pattern_type: Behavioral (GoF); realised through the Django signal dispatcher (framework idiom)
participant_roles: Subject=django.db.models.signals.post_save (a django.dispatch.Signal instance supplied by Django; attach through connect()/@receiver, notify through send()); ConcreteSubject=canteenapp.models.Item (sender; Item.save() derives is_available from count and calls Model.save(), whose save_base() sends post_save); Observer=not separately declared (Django receiver protocol: a callable taking sender, instance and **kwargs); ConcreteObserver=canteenapp.signals.remove_unavailable_item_from_cart (module-level function, not a class); Registration=canteenapp.apps.CanteenappConfig.ready() imports canteenapp.signals so the @receiver decorator connects the function; State changed by the observer=canteenapp.models.Cart rows; Notification triggers=item.save() in Order.create_order_from_cart (stock decrement at checkout) and in views.adminupdateitem, adminupdateitemimage, restaurantupdateitem, restaurantupdateitemimage

intent_and_evidence: Problem: when an item's stock count reaches zero it becomes unavailable, and carts that still contain it must be cleaned without every item-editing view knowing about carts. Evidence: Item.save() (models.py:144-149) sets is_available=False when count==0 and then calls super().save(); Django sends post_save after the row is written. @receiver(post_save, sender='canteenapp.Item') at signals.py:52 subscribes remove_unavailable_item_from_cart, which runs Cart.objects.filter(item=instance).delete() when the item is unavailable (signals.py:56-57). CanteenappConfig.ready() (apps.py:7-8) imports the module so the subscription exists at start-up. Checkout (Order.create_order_from_cart, models.py:339-358) and the four item-update views only call item.save() and contain no cart-cleanup code, so the subject does not know its observer. Abstract Subject and Observer roles are framework-supplied; there is one concrete observer.

intent_and_evidence: Problem: one order change must refresh several role-specific live dashboards (administrator, restaurant, delivery staff) without the view tracking open WebSocket connections. Evidence: each consumer's connect() checks the user's role and calls group_add for its group (consumers.py:355, 468, 595); disconnect() calls group_discard. adminupdateorderstatus validates the transition, saves the order (views.py:2168-2169) and calls group_send eight times with type keys such as admin_all_order and delivery_new_order (2170-2218). Channels dispatches each event to the consumer method named by type (for example AdminOrderConsumer.admin_all_order, consumers.py:365-371), which re-queries orders and sends JSON to the browser. Notifiers name only groups, never consumer classes. Classified as Observer in its publish-subscribe form: GoF lists Publish-Subscribe as an alias and describes a ChangeManager that holds the subject-observer mapping. It is not the strict form in which a subject object stores and calls its observers: there is no application Subject class, events are dictionaries, delivery is asynchronous, and the in-memory layer works only within one process.
